vulnerability.title: Configure opensc Smart Card Drivers
vulnerability.description: The OpenSC smart card tool can auto-detect smart card drivers; however, setting the smart card drivers in use by your organization helps to prevent users from using unauthorized smart cards. The default smart card driver for this profile is . To configure the OpenSC driver, edit the /etc/opensc.conf and add the following line into the file in the app default block, so it will look like: app default { ... card_drivers = ; }
vulnerability.recommendation: Remediation script: # Remediation is applicable only in certain platforms if rpm --quiet -q kernel-core; then var_smartcard_drivers='' OPENSC_TOOL="/usr/bin/opensc-tool" if [ -f "${OPENSC_TOOL}" ]; then ${OPENSC_TOOL} -S app:default:card_drivers:$var_smartcard_drivers fi else >&2 echo 'Remediation is not applicable, nothing was done' fi

triage_decision.reason: The remediation requires only a simple edit to /etc/opensc.conf or execution of a small script, which does not affect critical services or user authentication mechanisms beyond smart card usage. It is unlikely to cause lockout or system breakage.

concerns: The parsing logic must correctly handle nested blocks and comments; a syntax error could corrupt the config. No validation of file permissions or ownership is performed. The plan does not handle the scenario where multiple app default blocks exist.
suggested_improvements: Implement a backup step (e.g., cp /etc/opensc.conf /etc/opensc.conf.bak) before making changes. Use robust file parsing (e.g., awk or sed) that guarantees correct block detection and comment handling. Validate that the inserted line matches OpenSC syntax and that no trailing whitespace issues occur. If the app default block is missing, the script should add the entire block with default settings and the card_drivers line. After editing, run opensc-tool -S app:default:card_drivers:'' to verify configuration. Ensure file permissions remain root:root and mode 600. Add error handling for read/write failures. If multiple app default blocks exist, decide on a strategy (e.g., modify the first or merge).
